Volume is summed across the primary and every sibling, so the loop at `sib` (CauldronHook.sol:1602) costs one full 24-bucket sum per sibling and is bounded only by the sibling cap. A pluggable checker is consulted inside try/catch at `checker` (CauldronHook.sol:1607) and a revert falls back to the built-in comparison, so a broken module cannot brick relaunch — but a WORKING hostile module can return either answer.

nodes.name: _getCurrentBucket
nodes.signature: function _getCurrentBucket() private view returns (uint256)
nodes.reachability: Private view, one call site at `_getCurrentBucket` (CauldronHook.sol:1492). Pure wall-clock arithmetic on the block timestamp, which is what makes the window mean the same thing on a chain whose block numbers track a parent chain.

nodes.name: _getHolderTaxRate
nodes.signature: function _getHolderTaxRate(address holder) private view returns (uint256)
nodes.reachability: Private view, one call site at `_getHolderTaxRate` (CauldronHook.sol:1439). With no tier contract wired it returns the flat default. Otherwise it makes an unbounded-gas external view call inside try/catch at `INFTContract` (CauldronHook.sol:1627); a revert falls back to the default, but a returned rate is used VERBATIM with no cap of its own — the only ceiling is the combined clamp at `MAX_TOTAL_FEE_BPS` (CauldronHook.sol:1442).

nodes.name: setDefaultTaxBps
nodes.signature: function setDefaultTaxBps(uint256 _bps) external onlyOwner
nodes.reachability: Owner-only, bounded by `MAX_TAX_BPS` (CauldronHook.sol:1637) at ten percent. Only affects swaps where `nftContract` (CauldronHook.sol:1625) is unset or reverting.

nodes.name: releaseRelaunchETH
nodes.signature: function releaseRelaunchETH() external returns (uint256 amount)
nodes.reachability: Registry-only, and the counter is zeroed BEFORE the send at `relaunchETH` (CauldronHook.sol:1657), so it is checks-effects-interactions. A zero balance reverts `NoETHToRelease` (CauldronHook.sol:1655) rather than returning zero, and a failed send reverts `SendFailed` (CauldronHook.sol:1660) — which rolls the zeroing back, so the counter and the balance cannot silently diverge here. The counter is authoritative: nothing compares it against `address(this).balance`, so ether paid out elsewhere reduces the backing without reducing the number.

nodes.name: releaseRelaunchAsset
nodes.signature: function releaseRelaunchAsset(address asset) external returns (uint256 amount)
nodes.reachability: Registry-only, per-asset counterpart to the native release. The mapping entry is zeroed before the move at `relaunchAsset` (CauldronHook.sol:1685) and the library's boolean IS checked at `send` (CauldronHook.sol:1686), so a token that returns false rather than reverting cannot zero the counter while the tokens stay put. The gas cap passed is zero, i.e. unbounded, which matters only for the native branch the caller cannot reach here.

nodes.name: setDeathThreshold
nodes.signature: function setDeathThreshold( uint256 _threshold, address _oracle, uint256 _volumePerNFT, uint256 _nftPriceStep, uint256 _oddsFullVolume ) external onlyOwner
nodes.reachability: Owner-only, and the only way to wire `quoteOracle` (CauldronHook.sol:1747). Wiring an oracle re-denominates every volume-derived number, so the setter forces the curve to be restated in the same call and rejects a zero base or zero full-play size at `BadParam` (CauldronHook.sol:1746). A zero oracle argument leaves the oracle and the curve untouched while still moving `deathThreshold` (CauldronHook.sol:1744) — and there is no way to UNSET an oracle once set, because address(0) is the leave-alone sentinel.

nodes.name: forceClosePerps
nodes.signature: function forceClosePerps() external
nodes.reachability: Registry-only, called once per rebirth. It raises the transient relaunch flag at `_inRelaunchClose` (CauldronHook.sol:1764) so the engine's settlement swaps skip fee and buyback, force-closes inside try/catch, then lowers it at `_inRelaunchClose` (CauldronHook.sol:1766). The flag is transient, so it clears at end of transaction even if the close reverts. The final survivor check at `openCount` (CauldronHook.sol:1791) is NOT guarded and reverts `PerpsOpen` (CauldronHook.sol:1791) on any leftover, which deliberately unwinds the caller's whole relaunch rather than stranding positions.

nodes.name: setLiveKey
nodes.signature: function setLiveKey(PoolKey calldata k) external
nodes.reachability: Registry-only, pushed at every summon and relaunch. It is a plain storage write with NO validation of the key at `_liveKey` (CauldronHook.sol:1824) — not the currencies, not the fee, not the hook field — so the registry alone decides which pool the buyback spends into and which currency1 the credit gate at `_liveKey` (CauldronHook.sol:858) compares against.

nodes.name: liveKey
nodes.signature: function liveKey() external view returns (PoolKey memory)
nodes.reachability: External view returning the whole struct; the canonical pool for integrators. Same data the internal paths read at `_liveKey` (CauldronHook.sol:1028).

nodes.name: setLegacyBuyback
nodes.signature: function setLegacyBuyback(address registry_, uint256 bps, uint256 threshold) external
nodes.authority_gate_quote: if (msg.sender != registry && msg.sender != owner()) revert OnlyRegistry(); (CauldronHook.sol:1836)
nodes.reachability: Two holders: the registry and the owner. `legacyRegistry` (CauldronHook.sol:1838) is unvalidated and doubles as the authority for `sweepLegacyReserve` (CauldronHook.sol:1112), so setting it grants that withdrawal right to an arbitrary address. The share is bounded by `BPS` (CauldronHook.sol:1837) at 100 percent of the post-guild fee, and a zero threshold argument leaves the existing threshold alone at `legacyThreshold` (CauldronHook.sol:1840).

nodes.name: setDeathChecker
nodes.signature: function setDeathChecker(address _checker) external
nodes.authority_gate_quote: if (msg.sender != registry && msg.sender != owner()) revert OnlyRegistry(); (CauldronHook.sol:1850)
nodes.reachability: Owner or registry. Unvalidated: any address, including one that is not a contract, can be written to `deathChecker` (CauldronHook.sol:1851); the consumer wraps it in try/catch at `checker` (CauldronHook.sol:1607) so a bad module degrades to the built-in rule.

nodes.name: setPolicies
nodes.signature: function setPolicies(address _surtax, address _odds, address _curve) external
nodes.authority_gate_quote: if (msg.sender != registry && msg.sender != owner()) revert OnlyRegistry(); (CauldronHook.sol:1860)
nodes.reachability: Owner or registry; all three modules are written unconditionally, so passing address(0) for one CLEARS it rather than leaving it alone. Each consumer clamps and falls back: the surtax at `MAX_SNIPE_BPS` (CauldronHook.sol:1369), the odds at `ODDS_HARD_CAP_BPS` (CauldronHook.sol:2145), the curve at `c` (CauldronHook.sol:2096) which only rejects a zero price.

nodes.name: setFeeRouter
nodes.signature: function setFeeRouter(address _router) external
nodes.authority_gate_quote: if (msg.sender != registry && msg.sender != owner()) revert OnlyRegistry(); (CauldronHook.sol:1872)
nodes.reachability: Owner or registry. The router only returns amounts — the hook keeps custody and does the sends itself at `routeSplit` (CauldronHook.sol:1354) — and a result that does not sum exactly to the fee is discarded at `feeAmount` (CauldronHook.sol:1280). It is still a call made mid-swap into an admin-chosen address, so it is a re-entrancy surface into the fee path.

nodes.name: setNftContract
nodes.signature: function setNftContract(address _nft) external onlyOwner
nodes.reachability: Owner-only, unvalidated. It selects the contract every swap asks for a tax tier at `INFTContract` (CauldronHook.sol:1627), so it directly controls what every trader pays, bounded only by the combined clamp at `MAX_TOTAL_FEE_BPS` (CauldronHook.sol:1442).

nodes.name: setRegistry
nodes.signature: function setRegistry(address _registry) external onlyOwner
nodes.reachability: Owner-only and ONE-SHOT: a second call reverts `RegistryAlreadySet` (CauldronHook.sol:1891) and zero is rejected at `ZeroAddress` (CauldronHook.sol:1892). This is what stops the owner re-pointing the reserve's payee; the only way past it is the delayed override pair.

nodes.name: proposeRegistryOverride
nodes.signature: function proposeRegistryOverride(address _registry) external onlyOwner
nodes.reachability: Owner-only step one of the controller swap. It arms `pendingRegistry` (CauldronHook.sol:1908) and stamps a deadline of now plus the constant at `REGISTRY_SWAP_DELAY` (CauldronHook.sol:1909); the delay is a constant, so the owner cannot shorten their own notice period. Re-proposing simply overwrites both and restarts the clock.

nodes.name: cancelRegistryOverride
nodes.signature: function cancelRegistryOverride() external onlyOwner
nodes.reachability: Owner-only abort of an armed swap; no delay, because it can only ever cancel. It emits the proposal event with zero values at `RegistryOverrideProposed` (CauldronHook.sol:1918), which an indexer must interpret as a cancellation rather than a proposal.

nodes.name: executeRegistryOverride
nodes.signature: function executeRegistryOverride() external onlyOwner
nodes.reachability: Owner-only step two, refused before the deadline at `registrySwapReadyAt` (CauldronHook.sol:1929) — reusing the RegistryAlreadySet error for a timing condition. The whole native reserve is flushed to the OUTGOING registry first, zeroed before the send at `relaunchETH` (CauldronHook.sol:1932), and a failed send reverts the entire swap at `SendFailed` (CauldronHook.sol:1934). The per-asset reserves in `relaunchAsset` (CauldronHook.sol:1685) are NOT flushed, so a non-native reserve survives the controller change and can then only be pulled by the NEW registry.

nodes.name: setCollection
nodes.signature: function setCollection(address _collection) external
nodes.reachability: Registry-only, once per summon or relaunch. The external `totalMinted` (CauldronHook.sol:1965) read is NOT guarded, so a collection that reverts there blocks the whole wiring. Bumping `creditEpoch` (CauldronHook.sol:1966) namespaces credit so the previous generation's balances cannot mint the new collection, and the baseline anchors the rising curve at position zero even for a continued collection.

nodes.name: _wireLiquidator
nodes.signature: function _wireLiquidator(address _collection) private
nodes.reachability: Private; reached from `_wireLiquidator` (CauldronHook.sol:1969) and `_wireLiquidator` (CauldronHook.sol:2014). Best-effort: the try/catch at `ICollectionLiquidator` (CauldronHook.sol:1982) means a collection that does not grant the hook this right cannot brick a summon, and equally means a silent failure to wire badges.

nodes.name: setVault
nodes.signature: function setVault(address _vault) external
nodes.reachability: Registry-only, unvalidated. `vault` (CauldronHook.sol:1988) is a payee: the native floor share is sent there at `routeSplit` (CauldronHook.sol:1354), and clearing it to zero reroutes that share to the legacy buffer or the reserve at `vault` (CauldronHook.sol:1336).

nodes.name: setQuest
nodes.signature: function setQuest(address _quest) external
nodes.authority_gate_quote: if (msg.sender != registry && msg.sender != owner()) revert OnlyRegistry(); (CauldronHook.sol:1993)
nodes.reachability: Owner or registry, unvalidated. The quest contract is called mid-swap with ignored result at `quest` (CauldronHook.sol:907), but with NO gas cap — unlike the seeder and perp calls — so a hostile quest can burn the swapper's remaining gas.

nodes.name: setSeeder
nodes.signature: function setSeeder(address _seeder) external
nodes.authority_gate_quote: if (msg.sender != registry && msg.sender != owner()) revert OnlyRegistry(); (CauldronHook.sol:2002)
nodes.reachability: Owner or registry, unvalidated. Setting it turns on the in-swap poke at `s` (CauldronHook.sol:1052); clearing it to zero turns the in-swap nudge off at `s` (CauldronHook.sol:1049) without disabling the seeder's own permissionless path.

nodes.name: setPerpEngine
nodes.signature: function setPerpEngine(address _engine) external
nodes.authority_gate_quote: if (msg.sender != registry && msg.sender != owner()) revert OnlyRegistry(); (CauldronHook.sol:2010)
nodes.reachability: Owner or registry, unvalidated. This single slot controls four behaviours: the in-swap sweep at `perpEngine` (CauldronHook.sol:945), the perp fee route at `perpEngine` (CauldronHook.sol:1465), the open-positions interlock at `perpEngine` (CauldronHook.sol:1564), and the relaunch force-close at `perpEngine` (CauldronHook.sol:1762). Zeroing it disables all four at once.

nodes.name: setFloorBps
nodes.signature: function setFloorBps(uint256 _bps) external onlyOwner
nodes.reachability: Owner-only, bounded at 100 percent by `BPS` (CauldronHook.sol:2019). It splits the post-guild fee between the floor vault and the relaunch reserve at `floorBps` (CauldronHook.sol:1290).

nodes.name: setGuild
nodes.signature: function setGuild(address _guild) external
nodes.authority_gate_quote: if (msg.sender != registry && msg.sender != owner()) revert OnlyRegistry(); (CauldronHook.sol:2026)
nodes.reachability: Owner or registry, unvalidated. `guild` (CauldronHook.sol:2027) is the recipient of the off-the-top tribute at `guild` (CauldronHook.sol:1288) AND of 100 percent of every anti-sniper surtax at `guild` (CauldronHook.sol:1473), so this one slot can redirect the single largest fee stream at launch.

nodes.name: setGuildBps
nodes.signature: function setGuildBps(uint256 _bps) external onlyOwner
nodes.reachability: Owner-only. The cap is the hard-coded deployed default at `BadParam` (CauldronHook.sol:2038), so the share can be lowered and restored but never raised above it.

nodes.name: setActiveProposer
nodes.signature: function setActiveProposer(address who) external
nodes.authority_gate_quote: if (msg.sender != registry && msg.sender != owner()) revert OnlyRegistry(); (CauldronHook.sol:2046)
nodes.reachability: Owner or registry, unvalidated. The named address accrues a pull-only balance at `proposerOwed` (CauldronHook.sol:1262) on every NATIVE fee; address(0) disables the slice for that iteration at `prop` (CauldronHook.sol:1259).

nodes.name: setProposerBps
nodes.signature: function setProposerBps(uint256 _bps) external onlyOwner
nodes.reachability: Owner-only, capped at `MAX_PROPOSER_BPS` (CauldronHook.sol:2053) so the slice can never cannibalise the floor or the guild.

nodes.name: claimProposerFees
nodes.signature: function claimProposerFees() external nonReentrant returns (uint256 amount)
nodes.authority: anyone (each caller can only claim their own accrued balance)
nodes.reachability: Permissionless pull. Guarded by `nonReentrant` (CauldronHook.sol:2060) and written checks-effects-interactions: the balance is zeroed at `proposerOwed` (CauldronHook.sol:2063) before the value-bearing call. An empty balance reverts `NoETHToRelease` (CauldronHook.sol:2062). The ether paid out is the hook's raw balance, which is the same balance backing `relaunchETH` (CauldronHook.sol:1654) and `legacyBuffer` (CauldronHook.sol:1065) — none of those counters is reconciled against the balance.
nodes.value: sends native to the caller via `call` (line 2064)

nodes.name: setNftCurve
nodes.signature: function setNftCurve(uint256 _base, uint256 _step) external onlyOwner
nodes.reachability: Owner-only; the only bound is a non-zero base at `BadParam` (CauldronHook.sol:2071). It restates the crystal ladder that `volumePerNFT` (CauldronHook.sol:2099) prices against, in whatever unit the volume ledger currently uses.

nodes.name: setCreditUntaggedSwaps
nodes.signature: function setCreditUntaggedSwaps(bool on) external onlyOwner
nodes.reachability: Owner-only single-slot toggle. When off, an untagged direct swap credits nobody at `creditUntaggedSwaps` (CauldronHook.sol:876) and therefore also skips the in-swap gacha, since that path only arms for an untagged buyer.

nodes.name: setNftCurveFrom
nodes.signature: function setNftCurveFrom(uint256 _base) external
nodes.reachability: Registry-only, called from a winning proposal's parameters. A zero argument is a no-op at `_base` (CauldronHook.sol:2085) rather than an error, and it forces a FLAT ladder by zeroing the step at `nftPriceStep` (CauldronHook.sol:2087), which is how a mint-out volume target is made exact.

nodes.name: nftPriceAt
nodes.signature: function nftPriceAt(uint256 k) public view returns (uint256)
nodes.reachability: Public view, and on the commit path from `nftPriceAt` (CauldronHook.sol:2238) — once per crystal, so up to 30 external calls per commit when a curve policy is wired. A policy result of zero is rejected at `c` (CauldronHook.sol:2096) because a free crystal would mint without bound, but there is no UPPER bound on what a policy may charge.

nodes.name: creditOf
nodes.signature: function creditOf(address player) external view returns (uint256)
nodes.reachability: External view of the current epoch's balance only; credit from a previous generation still sits in `nftCredit` (CauldronHook.sol:892) under an older epoch key and is unreadable through this getter.

nodes.name: _curvePos
nodes.signature: function _curvePos() internal view returns (uint256)
nodes.reachability: Internal view; three callers, all views, each of which has already checked that a collection is set. The subtraction of `mintBaseline` (CauldronHook.sol:2113) is unguarded, so it underflows and reverts if the collection's minted count ever drops below the baseline recorded at wiring time.

nodes.name: crystalsReady
nodes.signature: function crystalsReady(address player) public view returns (uint256 ready)
nodes.reachability: Public view for the UI. The loop is bounded by the constant at `MAX_MINTS_PER_CALL` (CauldronHook.sol:2122), so it reports at most 30 even when the player can afford more, and each iteration may make an external policy call through `nftPriceAt` (CauldronHook.sol:2123).

nodes.name: costOfNextCrystals
nodes.signature: function costOfNextCrystals(uint256 count) public view returns (uint256 cost)
nodes.reachability: Public view. The loop bound is the CALLER-SUPPLIED `count` (CauldronHook.sol:2134) with no cap, so an off-chain caller can ask for an unbounded amount of work; it is a view, so the cost falls on the node answering the query, not on a transaction.

nodes.name: oddsForPlay
nodes.signature: function oddsForPlay(uint256 playWei) public view returns (uint256 bps)
nodes.reachability: Public view, also called once per commit at `oddsForPlay` (CauldronHook.sol:2255) and cast to uint16 there. A zero full-play size short-circuits to the maximum at `oddsFullVolumeWei` (CauldronHook.sol:2148). The linear scale rounds DOWN at `bps` (CauldronHook.sol:2149), so a play below one ten-thousandth of the full size rolls zero odds, and any policy answer is clamped to the hard cap.

nodes.name: outstandingTickets
nodes.signature: function outstandingTickets() external view returns (uint256)
nodes.reachability: External view over the GLOBAL counter, which spans every collection; the per-collection figure the pricing actually uses is `outstandingOf` (CauldronHook.sol:2113) and is not exposed by this getter.

nodes.name: mintedOut
nodes.signature: function mintedOut() external view returns (bool)
nodes.reachability: External view; two external calls, neither guarded, so a reverting collection makes this revert rather than report. It ignores the reserved crystals counted at `outstandingOf` (CauldronHook.sol:2226), so it can report not-minted-out while every remaining slot is already spoken for.

nodes.name: progress
nodes.signature: function progress(address player) external view returns (uint256 inCurrent, uint256 threshold, uint256 ready)
nodes.reachability: External view for the UI; duplicates the loop in `crystalsReady` (CauldronHook.sol:2117) and additionally prices the next unaffordable crystal at `threshold` (CauldronHook.sol:2184). Same 30-iteration bound.

nodes.name: commitCrystals
nodes.signature: function commitCrystals(address player, uint256 maxCount, uint256 playWei) external nonReentrant returns (uint256 n)
nodes.reachability: Only an allow-listed opener may call it, which is what keeps the play size honest — `playWei` (CauldronHook.sol:2196) is supplied by the caller and feeds the odds directly, so an unrestricted caller could claim any play size. Guarded by `nonReentrant` (CauldronHook.sol:2198), which shares one guard with the resolve path and the in-swap gacha. The player is also caller-supplied, so an opener can commit on anyone's behalf and spend THAT player's credit.

nodes.name: _commitCrystals
nodes.signature: function _commitCrystals(address player, uint256 maxCount, uint256 playWei) internal returns (uint256 n)
nodes.reachability: Shared body for the opener path and the in-swap native path. It never reverts on a sold-out collection: room is clamped to minted plus reserved at `room` (CauldronHook.sol:2227) and zero room returns zero. Pricing starts from minted PLUS reserved at `startPos` (CauldronHook.sol:2233) so concurrent commits do not share a curve slot. The affordability loop is bounded by the smaller of the caller's count and the 30-crystal constant. Five counters move together at `outstandingCrystals` (CauldronHook.sol:2252) and the batch is appended to an ever-growing array at `batches` (CauldronHook.sol:2256); nothing ever shrinks that array, only the cursor advances.

nodes.name: resolveTickets
nodes.signature: function resolveTickets(uint256 maxCount) public nonReentrant returns (uint256 processed, uint256 won)
nodes.reachability: Permissionless keeper entrypoint, guarded by `nonReentrant` (CauldronHook.sol:2278). The gacha router calls it right after committing, and anyone may call it at any time; the caller chooses `maxCount` (CauldronHook.sol:2276), which is the loop bound.

nodes.name: _resolveTickets
nodes.signature: function _resolveTickets(uint256 maxCount) internal returns (uint256 processed, uint256 won)
nodes.reachability: Two callers: the permissionless entry and the in-swap gacha. The outer loop walks the FIFO from `batchCursor` (CauldronHook.sol:2292) and stops without reverting at a batch committed this block at `commitBlock` (CauldronHook.sol:2296). An expired blockhash re-anchors the batch to the current block at `commitBlock` (CauldronHook.sol:2306) and breaks, preserving order; that write moves a batch FORWARD in time, so a batch can be re-anchored repeatedly. Both loops are bounded by the caller's maxCount. The roll is keccak over the commit blockhash, the player, the batch index and the ticket index at `roll` (CauldronHook.sol:2319), modulo 10000, so it is uniform only to the extent the blockhash is. A win mints through an external call at `mint` (CauldronHook.sol:2329) AFTER the three counters have been decremented, so the state is consistent before the callee runs; the same collection contract also controls whether that call reverts and unwinds the whole resolve.

nodes.name: nativeGachaStep
nodes.signature: function nativeGachaStep(address player, uint256 playWei) external nonReentrant
nodes.reachability: External but self-only; the sole reachable caller is the gas-capped self `call` (CauldronHook.sol:965) at the tail of afterSwap, whose result is discarded. `nonReentrant` (CauldronHook.sol:2350) shares the guard with the commit and resolve entrypoints, so a mint callback cannot re-enter either. The play size passed in is the weighted volume computed in afterSwap, i.e. already in the ledger's unit rather than raw ether.

nodes.name: setOpener
nodes.signature: function setOpener(address who, bool allowed) external
nodes.authority_gate_quote: if (msg.sender != registry && msg.sender != owner()) revert OnlyRegistry(); (CauldronHook.sol:2360)
nodes.reachability: Owner or registry. An opener gets three powers at once: it may commit crystals for any player at `isOpener` (CauldronHook.sol:2201), its hookData tag is believed for tax tiering at `isOpener` (CauldronHook.sol:2392), and its tag is believed for fee exemption at `isOpener` (CauldronHook.sol:2384).

nodes.name: setTaxExempt
nodes.signature: function setTaxExempt(address who, bool exempt) external
nodes.authority_gate_quote: if (msg.sender != registry && msg.sender != owner()) revert OnlyRegistry(); (CauldronHook.sol:2370)
nodes.reachability: Owner or registry. Exemption alone is not enough to dodge the fee: the swap must ALSO arrive from a trusted opener, per the conjunction at `isOpener` (CauldronHook.sol:2384), so a direct swapper cannot self-tag as exempt.

nodes.name: _isExemptPlayer
nodes.signature: function _isExemptPlayer(address sender, bytes calldata hookData) private view returns (bool)
nodes.reachability: Private view on both fee legs, at `_isExemptPlayer` (CauldronHook.sol:1167) and `_isExemptPlayer` (CauldronHook.sol:990). Exemption requires BOTH a flagged player and a trusted sender, so the hookData tag is only honoured from an opener.

nodes.name: _taxedPlayer
nodes.signature: function _taxedPlayer(address sender, bytes calldata hookData) private view returns (address)
nodes.reachability: Private view; the identity resolver used for both tiering at `_taxedPlayer` (CauldronHook.sol:1439) and exemption at `_taxedPlayer` (CauldronHook.sol:2384). A non-opener sender is always taxed as itself; an opener may name any player, and a zero decode falls back to the sender at `p` (CauldronHook.sol:2394).

nodes.name: setOddsParams
nodes.signature: function setOddsParams(uint256 fullVolumeWei, uint256 pity) external onlyOwner
nodes.reachability: Owner-only and UNBOUNDED on both arguments: `oddsFullVolumeWei` (CauldronHook.sol:2400) may be set to zero, which makes every play roll the maximum odds at `oddsFullVolumeWei` (CauldronHook.sol:2148), and `pityThreshold` (CauldronHook.sol:2401) may be set to zero, which makes every ticket a forced win at `forced` (CauldronHook.sol:2320).

nodes.name: setMaxOdds
nodes.signature: function setMaxOdds(uint256 bps) external onlyOwner
nodes.reachability: Owner-only, capped at `ODDS_HARD_CAP_BPS` (CauldronHook.sol:2407) so bet size alone can never guarantee a creature; only the pity counter can.

nodes.name: setWeights
nodes.signature: function setWeights(uint256 buyBps, uint256 sellBps) external onlyOwner
nodes.reachability: Owner-only, each side capped at `MAX_WEIGHT_BPS` (CauldronHook.sol:2413). These multiply the recorded volume into crystal credit at `buyWeightBps` (CauldronHook.sol:888), so raising them accelerates mint-out for every trader at once.

nodes.signature: receive() external payable
nodes.reachability: Empty payable fallback-style receiver. It records NOTHING, deliberately: ether arriving here — including the pool manager's payouts and any stray transfer — must not be counted into `legacyBuffer` (CauldronHook.sol:1097), which is why donations have their own entrypoint. Anything sent here silently increases the raw balance behind the counters without increasing any of them.

nodes.name: route
nodes.signature: function route(uint256 feeAmount, address guild, address vault, uint256 guildBps, uint256 floorBps) external pure returns (uint256 toGuild, uint256 toFloor, uint256 toRelaunch)
nodes.reachability: External `pure` (DefaultFeeRouter.sol:23) with no storage and no calls, so it is callable by anyone and can only return numbers. It is reached from the hook's fee path only if the timelock points `feeRouter` (CauldronHook.sol:1277) at this contract; the hook then calls it inside a try/catch at `route` (CauldronHook.sol:1279) and discards the result unless the three parts sum exactly to the fee. `toGuild` (DefaultFeeRouter.sol:26) and `toFloor` (DefaultFeeRouter.sol:28) are floor-divided by the constant, and `toRelaunch` (DefaultFeeRouter.sol:29) takes the remainder so the sum is exact by construction.

nodes.name: routeSplit
nodes.signature: function routeSplit( address asset, address guild, address vault, uint256 toGuild, uint256 toFloor ) external returns (uint256 leftover)
